title: Tourism service supply chains in ten emerging economies: data collection and analysis notebooks
description:
Notebooks documenting how a corpus of user-generated tourism reviews was retrieved from the Google Places API and how it was analysed, for a study of tourism service supply chains in ten emerging economies (51,037 reviews, 11,500 providers, 29 cities).

Contents. A collection notebook documenting the retrieval protocol, which runs in a dry-run mode issuing no API calls, and an analysis notebook implementing text normalisation, dictionary-based construct coding with negation handling, and logistic regressions with city fixed effects and supplier-clustered standard errors.

Data availability. The raw review corpus is NOT distributed and is NOT available on request. Google Maps Platform policies permit indefinite storage of place identifiers only; review text, author names, ratings and related Places content may not be pre-fetched, cached or retained outside the permitted exceptions, and may not be exported for use outside the Services. Reviewer display names were processed only for deduplication and appear in no released file. The collection notebook allows an independent researcher with their own API credentials to reconstruct an equivalent corpus; re-execution does not reproduce the same corpus, because the platform returns a relevance-ranked subset that changes continuously.

Measurement status. The coding dictionaries have NOT been validated against independent human coding. A held-out double-coded validation protocol was prepared but had not been executed at this version. No precision, sensitivity, specificity, F1 or inter-coder agreement statistics are reported. Construct prevalence is dictionary prevalence, not validated prevalence of the phenomenon. The collection-stratum labels have likewise not been audited at provider level.
